messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing repeated Xid 13 / ECC messages on a subset of eu-west-1 nodes the last 48h. GPU 0 shows a clear ECC counter delta. Dropping a tiny dmesg + nvidia-smi snapshot below for quick triage.

maria: ```
[ 1152.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1c: GPU 0): 13, pid=1987, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1152.123467] NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: Xid 13, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1153.987654] kernel: nvme_core: requeueing submission due to slot: 0
```

maria: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0000:01:00.0
    ECC Errors:
        Volatile: 0
        Aggregate: 124 (24 in last 24h)
Driver Version: 535.86.10
```

ajay: ugh, thanks for the snapshot. Can you also grab `journalctl -k -n 200` and `sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.volatile.aggregate --format=csv` for the node? low-noise bundle please.

elena: we should avoid full node bundles — they blow up storage. Proposal: a "microbundle" (200 lines dmesg, last 200 journalctl -k, nvidia-smi -q ECC, pciids + lspci -vv for slot info). gz and upload to customer-evidence-snapshots with 7d TTL.

sam: +1. Also include a tiny runtime metadata json (driver, kernel, pod list on node, card model, bios). That helps correlate with card-level flaky patterns. Example: `echo '{\"drv\":\"535.86.10\",\"kernel\":\"6.2.15\",\"slot\":\"0000:01:00.0\"}' > meta.json` then tar.gz everything.

node-health-bot: ALERT: eu-west-1a gpu-022 flagged: ECC aggregate delta > 15 in 24h. Suggested action: isolate, run burnin test.

ajay: for triage steps: 1) isolate pod(s) on that GPU 2) tail dmesg while repro test (small window) 3) collect microbundle if repro reproduces 4) if Xid persists after soft-reset, schedule drain/replace.

maria: quick commands I'm running now (paste to run locally):
`sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/microbundle/dmesg.txt`
`journalctl -k -n 200 --no-pager > /tmp/microbundle/journal-k.txt`
`nvidia-smi -q -d ECC > /tmp/microbundle/nvidia-ecc.txt`
`lspci -vv -s 01:00.0 > /tmp/microbundle/lspci-0100.txt`
`tar -czf /tmp/microbundle-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).tgz -C /tmp microbundle`

elena: I'll push a tiny helper script to infra-tools called `gpu-microbundle` that automates the above + adds node metadata and annotated S3 upload with tags `env:prod,region:eu-west-1a,reason:xid13`. Keeps bundles sub-10MB.

sam: what's our drain threshold again? I remember we used delta > 20 ECC in 24h + 2 Xid events on same slot to auto-schedule replacement.

maria: policy reminder: operator action is required at delta >= 15 *and* repeat Xid within 6h. If both true, prefer marking node for maintenance and live-migrate pods before eviction.

ajay: do we have a cheap quick repro? maybe run `cuda_memtest` or a small nvml stress for 5m to see if errors climb predictably. But do that on a drained node or during maintenance window.

elena: noted. I'll add a flag to the microbundle script to optionally run a non-destructive 60s memory scan and append nvml counters pre/post. Default off.

node-health-bot: NOTE: auto-attach_of_microbundle feature toggled off in prod. Manual upload for now.

maria: action items: elena -> push microbundle script + upload workflow (ETA today EOD). ajay -> collect microbundle for affected nodes and attach in the incident card. sam -> update maintenance playbook with the delta/Xid thresholds. I'll start draining node gpu-022 if we see another Xid within 6h.

elena: on it. Upload path I'll use: `s3://redwood-inference/gpu-microbundles/eu-west-1a/$(date +%F)/$(hostname)-$TS.tgz` with 7d lifecycle.

maria: thanks. keeping this short — we'll reconvene if microbundles show driver bug vs hardware. :thumbsup:
